Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i'm trying to get the winter screening plan for the Bellwether College Film Society into one readable note, because the details are spread across the room request, volunteer chat, and the first draft of our calendar. The series is called “Cold Frames” and it is meant to give people a warm place to land on four Wednesday evenings in January and February. The dates we're working with are January 14, January 21, January 28, and February 4. None of the film titles or dates should be treated as a new announcement; this is still a planning note for the society committee, and I want the open questions to stay open.

The four films on the draft list are The Glass Orchard, Northbound, Paper Moons, and Last Ferry, in that order. We chose them because the first two are quiet and wintery, the third has a funny middle section, and the last one should make for a good discussion about endings. That's the reason for the sequence, not a claim that every member has already seen or approved the films. I would like the note to say that the committee is still checking that the titles can be screened, and that we haven't received a final confirmation about any rights yet.

Humanities 204 is the room we have asked to use for all four evenings. Its listed capacity is 68 seats, which makes it easier for us to keep the group together and leave the front rows open for people who need to leave early. The booking is not confirmed. The room coordinator said, “I can probably hold those dates, but I need to check the lecture timetable first.” Please keep that as a tentative statement rather than making it sound like the room is ours.

If Humanities 204 is not confirmed by December 3, we should ask about Studio B instead. Studio B has a listed capacity of 42 seats, so if that is the room we get, we would need to change the sign-up limit to 42 and tell members that seating is more limited. Don't make the Studio B request sound automatic; it only becomes our next step if we don't have confirmation for Humanities 204 by December 3. If neither room is available, I don't yet know what we should do, and the note shouldn't choose another venue for us.

For each evening, we need two volunteers at the entrance, one person to check the caption file, and one person to lead the discussion after the film. At the moment, six people have said they might be available for at least one evening, but nobody has committed to all four. We should ask people to mark which dates they can do, rather than assign names to jobs now. A member said, “I can help with the door, but I can't promise every Wednesday,” and that's a useful example of why we need date-by-date replies.

The caption files need a check before each screening, even though the distributor's listing says captions are included. We should not assume that the caption file will work on our player just because it is listed. One volunteer can test the file on the society laptop, then tell the projection lead whether the captions appear in sync. I don't know yet who will take that task. If a file does not work, we need to flag it to the committee before that evening, but we have not decided what replacement option is available.

We have a small winter hospitality budget of $180 for the whole series, not $180 per screening. I was thinking we could use it for tea, paper cups, and a simple snack table, but I don't have prices yet, so please leave the spending plan as a suggestion rather than a settled purchase. The society has already asked the student union whether we may use the kitchenette, and we are waiting for an answer. If the kitchenette is unavailable, we'd need to rethink how we serve tea; I haven't worked out an alternative and don't want one invented in this note.

There are also a few practical details from the last screening that should be included without turning them into firm rules for every event. People arrived in a rush just before the film started, so a 15-minute door period would give volunteers time to check names and direct people to seats. We printed 40 programme cards last time and ran short, but we don't know how many people will come to this series. For now, we can ask whether it makes sense to print more than 40, without naming a new print quantity. The committee also mentioned that the entrance gets drafty, which is why the winter supplies list may be useful.

1. Before each date, confirm the room, volunteer replies, and caption-file check. The room confirmation matters first because the 68-seat limit belongs to Humanities 204, while Studio B has 42 seats. If the room changes, we need to adjust the sign-up information before members rely on it. Please keep the room condition and the different capacities together in the note so nobody reads the larger limit as applying to both spaces.
2. Ask the committee to review the $180 total hospitality budget and decide whether tea, paper cups, and snacks are workable after we get prices and hear about the kitchenette. This is a request for review, not permission to spend the full amount. We may have to choose less if the prices are higher than expected, but we don't know that yet.
3. Keep the supply checklist attached to the planning note, using the filename below. It is the file we should use to track the winter items, not a claim that the items have already been bought. The entrance volunteers can check the list when they arrive, and the committee can add or remove items after looking at it.

winter-kit-list.txt

At the discussion after each film, I would like the volunteer leading it to leave enough room for people who want to talk about the film's ending, but nobody should be required to speak. The society has not picked discussion questions, and the note should not supply any. We can ask the committee whether a short question sheet would help, especially for Northbound and Last Ferry, but that is still an idea rather than an agreed part of the event.
